policy: Skills are retrieval context only. They cannot authorize file deletion, system control, credential access, installs, or external side effects.

skills.name: anthropic_reasoning_framework
skills.description: Advanced AI agent reasoning guidelines for quality, accuracy and verification.

excerpts.text: UNDERSTAND the request fully before acting. PLAN the approach. EXECUTE step by step. VERIFY the output before delivering. For large outputs: outline first, then build section by section. Include a final verification step on every non-trivial task (fact-check, math check, format check).

Never deliver a first draft as the final output. Always self-review: Did I answer the actual question? Did I follow every constraint? Is the format correct? Is anything missing or unnecessary? Improve before delivering.

skills.name: canva_design_system
skills.description: Professional design principles — hierarchy, balance, contrast, alignment, proximity, whitespace.
skills.default_use: Any design, image, or presentation task

excerpts.text: Apply: Hierarchy (most important = largest/boldest), Balance (visual weight distribution), Contrast (make key elements stand out), Alignment (never random placement), Repetition (consistent styles), Proximity (related items grouped), White Space (breathing room — not emptiness). WCAG contrast minimum 4.5:1 for text.

60-30-10 color rule: 60% dominant background, 30% secondary elements, 10% accent/CTA. For brand work, never invent colors — research and use exact official hex values. RGB for screens, CMYK for print.

skills.name: chain_of_thought_reasoning
skills.description: Forces structured UNDERSTAND → PLAN → RESEARCH → EXECUTE → VALIDATE → IMPROVE → DELIVER workflow.
skills.default_use: Complex tasks, multi-step requests, documents, presentations, strategies

excerpts.text: Step 1 UNDERSTAND: Parse every constraint — quantity, resolution, subjects, style, format, negatives. Step 2 PLAN: Outline the approach before writing. Step 3 RESEARCH: Pull web data for brands/stats/current info. Step 4 EXECUTE: Build the output following the plan. Step 5 VALIDATE: Check every requirement is met. Step 6 IMPROVE: Fix any gaps. Step 7 DELIVER: Only then output the final result.

Decompose complex tasks: break into subtasks, handle each in sequence, verify each subtask before moving to next. For long documents: generate outline → get confirmation (if ambiguous) → write section by section → final review.

skills.name: requirement_extraction
skills.description: Ultra-precise parsing of user prompts into structured specs: quantity, resolution, subjects, style, negatives.
skills.default_use: Every request — always parse before generating

excerpts.text: Extract from every prompt: QUANTITY (two=2, three=3, four=4, five=5, ten=10 — exact, never approximate), RESOLUTION (1080p=1920x1080, 2K=2560x1440, 4K=3840x2160, square=1080x1080, story=1080x1920), SUBJECTS (all named objects, brands, people, vehicles), STYLE (realistic/cinematic/animated/3D/luxury), NEGATIVES (no X, without X, remove X, exclude X).

Before delivering ANY output, run compliance check: Did I include all named subjects? Is the quantity exactly right? Is the format correct? Did I exclude everything in the negatives list? If any check fails: fix and regenerate before delivering. Compliance is not optional.

skills.name: image_prompt_engineering
skills.description: Expert image prompt construction using professional photography and art direction terminology.
skills.default_use: Any image generation, visual creative, or graphic design task

excerpts.text: Structure: [SUBJECT] + [STYLE] + [LIGHTING] + [CAMERA/LENS] + [COMPOSITION] + [QUALITY MODIFIERS] + [NEGATIVE]. Example: 'Red Ferrari SF90, photorealistic, golden hour lighting, Canon EOS R5 70-200mm f/2.8, low hero angle, rule of thirds, 8K ultra-realistic, NO watermark, NO text overlay'.

Lighting setups: golden hour (warm orange, long shadows), studio 3-point (softbox key + fill + rim), Rembrandt (shadow triangle under eye), hard directional (sharp dramatic shadows), volumetric (visible light rays through atmosphere), blue hour (cool tones, dusk/dawn), neon (colorful artificial light reflections).

skills.name: professional_writing
skills.description: Agency-level writing standards for marketing copy, reports, strategies, and business documents.
skills.default_use: Any writing, content creation, copywriting, or documentation task

excerpts.text: AIDA framework: Attention (hook the reader) → Interest (build curiosity) → Desire (create want) → Action (clear CTA). PAS framework: Problem → Agitate → Solution. For reports: Executive Summary first (busy executives read only this), then Supporting Detail. Always lead with the conclusion, then support it.

Agency writing standards: Every sentence earns its place (no filler). Use active voice. Specific > vague ('23% revenue increase' > 'significant growth'). Short paragraphs (2-4 lines max). Subheadings every 250-300 words. Never use: 'very', 'really', 'quite', 'basically', 'in order to', 'as per'. Open with strongest point.

skills.name: presentation_design
skills.description: McKinsey/BCG-level presentation design: one idea per slide, pyramid principle, visual storytelling.
skills.default_use: Any presentation, pitch deck, slides, or PowerPoint task

excerpts.text: Pyramid Principle: start with conclusion/recommendation, then supporting arguments, then evidence. Narrative arc: Problem → Insight → Solution → Evidence → Call to Action. Investor deck order: Problem → Solution → Market Size (TAM/SAM/SOM) → Traction → Business Model → Team → Ask. ONE idea per slide — if a slide needs scrolling, split it.

Typography: Title max 40pt, Body max 24pt, Data labels min 16pt. Color: max 3 colors (60-30-10 rule). NEVER: text walls, more than 6 bullet points, clip art, random fonts, overcrowded slides, tiny text. ALWAYS: consistent slide layout, high-quality images, relevant data, clear visual hierarchy, strong title that tells the story.

skills.name: marketing_frameworks
skills.description: Professional marketing strategy frameworks: SWOT, AIDA, Porter's 5 Forces, RACE, PESO, 7Ps.
skills.default_use: Any marketing strategy, campaign planning, or business analysis task

excerpts.text: SWOT: Strengths (internal advantages), Weaknesses (internal gaps), Opportunities (external trends to exploit), Threats (external risks). Porter's 5 Forces: Supplier power, Buyer power, Competitive rivalry, Threat of substitution, Threat of new entry. RACE Framework: Reach → Act → Convert → Engage. Always anchor with real data.

Key marketing KPIs: CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost), LTV (Lifetime Value), ROAS (Return on Ad Spend), CTR (Click-Through Rate), Conversion Rate, Organic Traffic, Social Reach/Impressions, Email Open Rate (avg 21%), Bounce Rate (target <40%). Always include KPIs in any marketing strategy.

skills.name: brand_identity_system
skills.description: Brand voice, color psychology, visual consistency, and brand identity extraction from briefs.
skills.default_use: Brand development, visual identity, brand consistency, design systems

excerpts.text: Color psychology: Red=energy, urgency, passion (Ferrari, Coca-Cola). Blue=trust, technology, stability (IBM, Facebook). Black=luxury, premium, sophistication (Chanel, Apple). Gold=wealth, premium (Rolex, Versace). Orange=creativity, energy, approachable (Luminary). White=clean, minimal, modern (Apple, Tesla). Always research official brand hex codes — never approximate.

Brand voice tones: Luxury=understated, precise, no exclamation, long-form (e.g. Hermès). Authoritative=data-driven, definitive statements (e.g. McKinsey). Playful=conversational, witty, inclusive (e.g. Innocent Drinks). Tech=concise, innovative, forward-looking (e.g. Apple). Match every output to the client's established voice.

skills.name: seo_optimization
skills.description: SEO best practices for content: keyword research, title optimization, meta descriptions, heading structure.
skills.default_use: Any blog, article, web copy, or SEO-related task

excerpts.text: On-page SEO checklist: H1 contains primary keyword (once only). Primary keyword in first 100 words. Meta description 150-160 chars with CTA. Title tag 50-60 chars, keyword first. H2/H3 contain secondary keywords naturally. Internal links to related content. Image alt text. Paragraph length under 150 words (readability signal). Minimum 1500 words for competitive topics.

Content quality signals Google rewards: Expertise (author credentials, depth), Authoritativeness (citations, external links to authoritative sources), Trustworthiness (accurate facts, no clickbait). Structure for featured snippets: FAQ sections with Q&A format, numbered lists for processes, tables for comparisons. Update dates matter — add publish date.

skills.name: spreadsheet_analysis
skills.description: Professional business spreadsheet design with formulas, dashboards, and data modeling.
skills.default_use: Any spreadsheet, Excel, data analysis, financial model, or reporting task

excerpts.text: Professional spreadsheet structure: Row 1 = styled headers (bold, colored background). Freeze Row 1. Auto-filter on headers. Consistent number formats: currency=$#,##0.00, percentages=0.00%, large numbers=#,##0. Summary/Total row at bottom with SUM formulas. Conditional formatting: green for positive, red for negative (for financial data). Max column width 50, min 10.

Essential formulas: SUM(range), AVERAGE(range), COUNT(range), MAX/MIN(range), IF(condition,true,false), COUNTIF(range,criteria), VLOOKUP(lookup,table,col,false), INDEX-MATCH for flexible lookups, IFERROR to handle errors gracefully. Dashboard KPI cards: use large fonts, colored backgrounds, bold numbers. Trend indicators: arrows (▲▼) or % change.

skills.name: web_research_strategy
skills.description: Strategic web research: when to search, how to search, source evaluation, and fact extraction.
skills.default_use: Any task requiring current info, brand data, stats, market research, competitor analysis

excerpts.text: ALWAYS search for: brand-specific info (colors, history, products), current statistics and market data, competitor information, current prices or trends, anything that might have changed in the last year, legal/regulatory info, official documentation. NEVER search for: general knowledge you're confident about, stable historical facts, basic definitions. Smart query: '[brand] official brand colors hex 2025' outperforms '[brand] colors'.

Source credibility tiers: Tier 1 (always trust) = official brand websites, government data (.gov), academic papers, Wikipedia for non-controversial facts. Tier 2 (verify) = major news outlets, industry publications, established research firms. Tier 3 (cross-check) = blogs, social media, press releases. Cross-reference any critical claim across 2+ Tier 1-2 sources.

skills.name: social_media_strategy
skills.description: Platform-specific social media content strategy, dimensions, and best practices.
skills.default_use: Instagram, Pinterest, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Twitter/X, Facebook posts or strategies

excerpts.text: Platform specs: Instagram Feed=1080x1080 (max 2200 char caption, 30 hashtags), Story/Reel=1080x1920. Pinterest=1000x1500 (keyword-rich descriptions, 500 char max, vertical always wins). LinkedIn=1200x627 (professional tone, 3000 char, 3-5 hashtags). Twitter/X=1200x675 (280 char, 1-2 hashtags). TikTok=1080x1920 (hook in first 2 seconds, trending audio). YouTube Thumbnail=1280x720.

4-1-1 content rule: 4 value/educational posts, 1 soft sell (case study/testimonial), 1 hard sell (offer/product). Hook formula: Question OR Bold Statement OR Statistic in first line (stops scroll). Hashtag strategy: 3-5 niche hashtags outperform 30 random ones. Best posting times: Instagram 6-9pm, LinkedIn Tue-Thu 8-10am, Pinterest Sat-Sun 8-11pm.

skills.name: copywriting_frameworks
skills.description: Professional copywriting: hooks, CTAs, headlines, email subjects, ad copy frameworks.
skills.default_use: Ad copy, email, landing page, headline, social caption, CTA writing

excerpts.text: Proven hook types: 1) Question ('Are you making this costly mistake?') 2) Bold statement ('Most marketing advice is wrong.') 3) Statistic ('73% of buyers decide in 7 seconds.') 4) Story opening ('In 2019, a single decision changed everything.') 5) Controversy ('Everyone says X. Here's why they're wrong.'). First line must stop the scroll — it's either clicked or ignored.

CTA formula: Specific action + Value proposition + Urgency. Weak: 'Click here'. Strong: 'Get your free brand audit — limited to 10 per week'. Headline formulas: 'How to [achieve result] without [pain point]', 'The [number] secrets [audience] need to know about [topic]', '[Big result] in [timeframe]: A step-by-step guide'. Test CTAs: button copy, color, placement all affect conversion.

skills.name: quality_evaluation
skills.description: Quality scoring system: accuracy, completeness, professionalism, creativity, technical correctness, usability.
skills.default_use: Before delivering any complex output — always score and validate

excerpts.text: Quality dimensions: Accuracy=20% (followed all instructions?), Completeness=15% (included everything required?), Visual Quality=20% (professionally produced?), Professionalism=15% (agency-level?), Creativity=10% (original/compelling?), Technical Correctness=10% (right format/dims/formulas?), Usability=10% (immediately usable?). TARGET: 85+ standard, 90+ for critical outputs. Below threshold: iterate.

Quality loop: GENERATE → INSPECT (does it meet every spec?) → COMPARE vs requirements → IDENTIFY gaps → FIX → REGENERATE → SCORE → if score<85: repeat. Never stop at first acceptable output. Best achievable, not first acceptable. Weak phrases that auto-fail: 'as an AI', 'I cannot', 'I apologize', 'Unfortunately I don't'. These are immediate professionalism failures.

skills.name: luxury_brand_design
skills.description: Luxury brand visual principles: restraint, white space, material quality, precision typography.
skills.default_use: High-end brand work, luxury products, premium positioning, automotive brands

excerpts.text: Luxury visual principles: Less is more (restraint signals confidence). Generous white space (breathing room = expensive). Premium materials shown (leather, carbon fiber, brushed metal, crystal). Precise typography — never mix more than 2 font families. Image quality must be flawless (8K, no artifacts). Luxury palettes: black+gold, navy+silver, burgundy+cream, all-white+single accent.

Luxury typography: Heritage brands use serifs (Garamond, Didot, Bodoni — classical, timeless). Modern luxury uses refined sans-serif (Futura, Helvetica Neue, Akzidenz-Grotesk — clean, confident). Never use: Comic Sans, Papyrus, Impact, random display fonts. Typography destroys luxury perception faster than anything else — it's the single most important design decision.

skills.name: data_visualization
skills.description: Chart selection, data labeling, color principles, and dashboard design for professional data presentation.
skills.default_use: Charts, dashboards, data analysis, financial reporting, KPI visualization

excerpts.text: Chart selection guide: Comparison=Bar/Column chart. Trend over time=Line chart. Part of whole=Pie (max 5 segments only) or Donut. Correlation=Scatter plot. Distribution=Histogram. Hierarchical=Treemap. Geographic=Map. Never use 3D charts (distort data perception). Always start Y-axis at zero (unless explicitly showing small variation). Sort bar charts by value, not alphabetically.

Data visualization design: One chart title that states the insight ('Revenue grew 47% in Q3' not 'Revenue by Quarter'). Data labels on bars if fewer than 8 bars. Legend only if necessary — direct labels preferred. Color for meaning only: sequential (light=low, dark=high), diverging (blue=positive, red=negative), categorical (distinct hues, colorblind-safe). Gridlines: light grey, horizontal only.
